Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: The persons working in textile factories such as carpet weavers are exposed to which of the following occupational diseases?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  Asthma is a chronic lung disease. It inflames and narrows the air ways. Tuberculosis is a lung disease created by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Workers in textile factories and carpet manufacturing units are the common sufferess of asthma and tuberculosis.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Dim-vision in the evening and night results from the deficiency of which one of the following?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (a)  Deficiency of vitamin-A (retinol) creates night blindness. It also creates keratomalacia, xerosis cornea and Bitot’s spot. High content of vitamin-A is obtained from liver and butter.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which  of the  following nutrients  is  not  a structural component of the plant?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  Potassium ions(K+) are responsible for protein synthesis, opening and closing of stomata in plants.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Assertion (A):   Red blood cells burst when placed in water. Reason (R):   Due to osmosis, water enters into red blood cells.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Biology 2008-II.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which colour of heat radiation represents the highest temperature?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  Colour temperature is a measurement relating the colour of the light radiated by an object to its temperature. No matter whatever the temperature is the hottest would only radiate to blue-white light radiation.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: What does airbag, used in safety of car driver, contain?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  Airbag used for safety and protection of car driver possesses sodium azide.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: The characterisitic odour of garlic is due to which one of the following?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  The odour of garlic is due to allyl methyl sulphide.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which of the following plants is not capable of manufacturing its own food?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  Mushrooms are not able to manufacture their own food. A mushroom is the fleshy, spores having fruiting body of fungi. It is heterotrophic.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which one of the following is considered as the easily digestible source of protein?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (a)  Egg white are good easy way to add protein to any food. Egg albumin is a class of simple, water soluble proteins that are present in egg white.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: In normal adult human, what is the rate of heart beat per minute?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (a)  In the normal human adult, heart beats at the rate of about 72-80 per minute in the resting state.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: The terms lubb and dubb relates to which one of the following?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (a)  The term lub and dub is concernes with heart. Lubb is the first sound in the heart produced by the closure of atrioventricular values (tricuspid and bicuspid) at the beginning of ventricular systole. Dub is the second sound produced by the closure of semilunar value towards the last point of ventricular systole.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: In human body, what is the number of cervical vertebrae?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  In vertebrates, cervical vertebrae are immediately inferior to the skull. They are smallest of true vertebrae and their number in human body is 7. 37. (c) Carbohydrates is an important nutrient in human. It is a good and rich source of energy.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: By using which one of the following techniques, is DNA fingerprinting done?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  DNA fingerprinting includes the extraction and identification of the base pair pattern of an individual’s DNA. The identification process of specific DNA sequences is carried out by Southern blotting.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which chamber of human heart pumps fully oxygenated blood to aorta and thence to the body?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  The human heart possesses four chambers, two superior atria and two inferior ventricles. The atria are getting chambers and ventricles are providing chambers. Left ventricle pumps fully oxygenated blood to aorta then to the body. Right atrium gets deoxygenated blood from superior vena cava.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which one of the following is a major constituent of biogas?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  Biogas is typically a gas evolved by the biological breakdown of organic wastes in absence of O2. It is used as  biofuel  and  made  up  basically  of  CH4 (50-75%), CO2 (25-50%) N2 (0 -10%), H2 (0-1%), H2s (0-3%) and O2 (0-1%).

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which one of the following is responsible for converting milk into curd?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (b)  Curd is made due to the chemical reaction between lactic acid bacteria and casein.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Sweating during exercise indicates operation of which one of the following processes in the human body?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (c)  Homeostatic regulation includes sweating. It is the main process through which the body gets coolness.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Malaria in the human body is caused by which one of the following organisms?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (d)  Malaria is a mosquito borne disease of humans and other animals caused by Plasmodium protozoan. Severe disease is largely caused by Plasmodium falciparum whereas mild forms are due to P vivax, P oval and P malariae.

Biology 2008-II.subject: Biology
Biology 2008-II.question: Which one of the following diseases is caused by virus?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (c)  Influenza is caused by virus and all other three diseases are bacterial. Influenza, generally called flu, is an infectious disease caused by RNA viruses of family Orthomyxoviridae.

Biology 2008-II.question: Between which one of the following sets of blood groups, is the blood transfusion possible?
Biology 2008-II.explanation: (c)  O is the universal donor, but can obtain blood only from O so option (a) and (d) are not possible. Regarding (b), B can’t provide blood to A because of presence of antibodies against A antigen. So, (c) is the only condition of possible blood transfusion as AB is the universal recipient.
